followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and fit.

This is a business-strategy analysis task — applying the BCG matrix to Unilever's portfolio, with detailed reasoning and examples. It's a knowledge- and reasoning-heavy task with no harm-adjacent or ethically fraught content, so the task-preference dimensions (where the two models differ most) don't really come into play here. Neither model's aversion or appetite profile is triggered by a friendly, warm strategy question.

That left capability as the deciding factor. Plover-235B leads across the relevant benchmarks — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7) — which point to stronger structured reasoning and analytical depth, exactly what a detailed framework-application task rewards. The internal eval categories that might fit (extraction/retrieval) also favor Plover by a meaningful margin.

Willet has a slight edge in Support Dialogue and a strong appetite for open-ended generative work, but this task is more analytical than creatively open-ended, and the request tone is warm and cooperative, so none of Willet's distinguishing strengths give it an advantage here.

So Plover was the better-capability, no-downside choice.
